mechanism_narrative: Home-confinement time-use is sticky: RESIDENTIAL printed +10.0 in the latest week, its highest reading of the four-week window, so home-based routines continue to crowd out discretionary out-of-home trips. RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean stays below its trailing mean of -31.8.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL moved 5.3 -> 9.1 -> 7.0 -> 10.0 across the four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or above -31.8 while weekly RESIDENTIAL stays at or above +7.0.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT closed at -23.4, its second crossing of the -20 level in four weeks, and the transit base underpins weekday retail footfall. A transit series held below -20 removes the commuting trips that generate midweek retail-and-recreation visits, so RETAIL_REC falls further over the following 14 days.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean below -20 in at least 2 of the last 4 weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT = -24.1 at t-2w and -23.4 at t-0w
fact:TRANSIT never exceeded -10.4 in the observed window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or above -31.8 even though TRANSIT stays below -20 in at least 2 of the next 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Essential-goods substitution: when GROCERY_PHARM holds at or above baseline in the same week RETAIL_REC sits below -30, household trips are being rerouted to essentials rather than discretionary destinations. The joint state predicts continued retail suppression, not recovery, within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM >= 0 and RETAIL_REC <= -30 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM = 3.9 at t-3w and 2.4 at t-1w while RETAIL_REC = -30.1 at t-1w
failure_condition: In weeks where GROCERY_PHARM >= 0 and RETAIL_REC <= -30, the following week's RETAIL_REC exceeds the current week's value in more than half of observations.

mechanism_narrative: Late April to mid May is the seasonal upswing of the pre-pandemic retail-and-recreation baseline. Because the target series is percent change from that baseline, an unchanged absolute level of activity mechanically yields a higher reading in the next 28 days than in the trailing 28 days.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-04-15 sits at the start of the spring baseline ramp
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean is at or below -31.8 while RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES show no further tightening relative to the observed window.

mechanism_narrative: Lockdown-regime ceiling: the joint condition RESIDENTIAL >= 7 with WORKPLACES <= -20 held in all four observed weeks. In that administrative regime retail capacity is capped, so the next-28-day RETAIL_REC mean cannot exceed the trailing 28-day mean of -31.8.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL >= 7 and WORKPLACES <= -20 in the latest week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL ranged 5.3 to 10.0 and WORKPLACES ranged -30.0 to -17.6 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean rises above -31.8 while RESIDENTIAL stays >= 7 and WORKPLACES stays <= -20 in every week of the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: Compliance fatigue under prolonged confinement: once RESIDENTIAL has held at or above 9, adherence decays and TRANSIT ticks up first. Any week-on-week TRANSIT gain of 5 points or more in that state is followed within 14 days by a RETAIL_REC recovery.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by >= 5 points versus the prior week while RESIDENTIAL >= 9
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -24.1 at t-2w to -16.0 at t-1w, a +8.1 swing, while RESIDENTIAL rose from 9.1 to 7.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline in the 14 days following a >= 5 point week-on-week TRANSIT gain that occurs while RESIDENTIAL >= 9.

mechanism_narrative: Parks-versus-retail trip substitution: PARKS collapsed to -31.1, its lowest reading of the window, while RESIDENTIAL peaked at 10.0. The joint state shows outdoor trips being absorbed by home time rather than displaced to commercial venues, so RETAIL_REC stays weak within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean <= -25 and RESIDENTIAL >= 7 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS = -31.1 at t-0w versus -21.4 at t-3w
fact:RESIDENTIAL = 10.0 at t-0w, its maximum of the four weeks
failure_condition: Weekly RETAIL_REC rises above -26.3 in the seven days following a week in which PARKS <= -25 and RESIDENTIAL >= 7.

mechanism_narrative: Stringency ratchet: every category except GROCERY_PHARM worsened in the final week, with RETAIL_REC dropping from -30.1 to -35.6 as RESIDENTIAL rose from 7.0 to 10.0 and WORKPLACES fell to -26.3. Retail responds to policy tightening with a 2-to-4-week lag, so the next 28-day mean is lower.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -30.1 at t-1w to -35.6 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL rose from 7.0 to 10.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean exceeds -31.8 even though RESIDENTIAL stays at or above 9.0 and WORKPLACES stays at or below -25.0 across the next four weeks.
